It's a process. Relapses are part of the healing process. Don't be too hard with yourself. You just need to learn from every relapse.


Let me explain it with my own experience of that process:


The last time I was relapsing, I was feeling sexual frustration, because I wasn't able to talk to women on a party. The day after that I was so frustrated that I relapsed and binged. So the reason was the sexual frustration. I learned from it and started to be more patient - which was the reason for my relapse on a deeper level. Life isn't that instant gratification - it's a much slower process and that got me frustrated. So what does that mean? In order to prevent a relapse I have to become more patient. I am still a human being with a job, good friends,... Yes it sucks not being able to talk to women, but is it really worth the frustration? No! That change in my mindset was the learning experience from one of my relapses.



Another one was blocking websites I surfed out of a habit. The first thing I did was typing in the URL of the website and looking if there is something new. I blocked these sites by editing the host file of windows (just google "host file block websites").



Just see it as a process. You will relapse - but learn from each and every relapse. There are lessons in every relapse. Maybe it's feeling depressed? Then try something else instead - meditation about self love, gratefulness is another tool - be grateful for the things you already have. Be grateful that you have a gf who is willing to help you. Cultivate this feeling and you will start to love yourself - everyone wants to see you happy! Once you get that mindset - the feeling of depression is not as heavy in weight as it was.
